words.meaning: Asking for something. He probably was by the wayside between the old Jericho and the new Roman Jericho. Mark gives his name Bartimaeus (#Mr 10:46). #Mt 20:30 mentions two. (Robertson's NT Word Pictures)
words.plain: Begging [Greek: epaiton] means asking for something — and the man's position by the wayside was strategic. He was likely between the old city of Jericho and the new Roman Jericho, where travelers had to pass. Beggars claimed their spots carefully. This man heard the crowd coming and called out immediately — he had learned to read the sound of opportunity.
